scene clearnightsky
There’s a certain something in the air tonight.
I speak not of fire or ash, nor the rising embers the eyes of laughing children gravitate to as they drift closer to the sky — but of sorrow and safety. Delight and dismay.
And I speak this all to you, of course. For you are the only one fit to recount this journey of yours or mine or whoever it belongs to.
I did something bad tonight.
I’ve been doing that a lot lately — getting pickier with the rules I follow and the ones I overlook...but I promise it’s all for a good reason!
You see, one day, I want to make the world a better place.
But one of the big issues with that is that “better” for one person has the potential to mean “worse” for another. And that’s the exact sort of thing I’d like to avoid if at all possible.

So, as inevitable or unlikely as it may be, I will trek through this sand for as long as I have to. Hoping that whatever my metal-detector of a mind can pick up along the coast is enough to make you happy.
But a little birdie tells me it won’t be before another shows up and swallows it whole.
These creatures will grow until they’re far larger than me.
But that’s not saying a lot as, right now, I don’t exist.
I am but a thought in your head or a passing desire.
I am the light of the moon and the shadow that follows closely behind you.
I am everything you’ve never wanted, but all you’ll ever need.
And sure as the sunshine, our lives are in bloom.
I will follow you always.
I simply can’t help it.
All of a sudden, I see heads tilting upward.
And a new light emerges from the darkest of nights.

: Attention, everyone!

: Your beloved and beautiful blonde bombshell, Ayane Amamiya, has returned from her fateful venture into the woods to remind you all that it is she who holds a claim on the teacher’s heart! No one else!
: Ayane!
: A...Ayane! You’re back!

: I was just taking a much-needed vacation, Maya. But now I’m back and better than ever.
scene uhhhhhhhscenegoeshere3

: Not that much by the look of things. But I guess that’s what I deserve for opening up my glorious return with a stake on Sensei’s heart.
: Ayane...are you seriously okay? You seem way too...chipper for someone who was just lost in the woods for a shocking amount of time.

scene uhhhhhhhscenegoeshere5

: Sensei, come on! Let’s go welcome Ayane back to the beach!
My adorable and loving niece, Ami Arakawa, grabs my hand and pulls me closer to Ayane — who is, very thankfully, still alive.

scene uhhhhhhhscenegoeshere9

scene uhhhhhhhscenegoeshere10

: Unless Miss Watabe decides to throw us under the bus for indecent exposure or whatever. But even then, Sensei will probably have to take the heat for all of it because he’s-

: Thank you, Uta. Please don’t...expect too much out of me, though. I don’t typically write horror and...
: And actually, even if I did, there probably wouldn’t be much to expect. I’m not very good. I just...like the act of writing.
: I’m sure that whatever you’ve come up with will be quite delightful, Futaba. Though, I am a bit of a connoisseur, so I will be judging you harshly. But I assure you I mean no offense.
: That...makes me a lot more confident. Thank you, Touka.
: No, Futaba. Thank you. For engaging in a competition that does not revolve around pleasing our teacher, but good, old fashioned fun. We need more of that around here.
: Maybe we can all get lost in the woods for the next Dorm Wars? Wouldn’t that be fun?
scene uhhhhhhhscenegoeshere15
: No. It most certainly would not be fun. And you are to never leave my side again. Now be a good girl and remain silent while Futaba reads her story.
scene uhhhhhhhscenegoeshere16
: Well, if...nobody else has anything to say...I guess I’ll start reading.
: Please do. We’re all very excited.
: Only if...nobody has anything else to say.
: No one has anything else to say.
: I’ll just give it a few more minutes before I-
: Just read the gosh darn story, Futaba.
: Touka’s getting angry again.
: Shush you. It’s scary time.
: This...story is called...uhh...
: The Ghost of the 63rd Floor...
scene clearnightsky
: A long, long time ago...back before cell phones and tablets existed...people needed to actually communicate with one another to pass the time...
: But this story begins in a town where that wasn’t possible.
: It was a small, countryside town. So small that you wouldn’t even be able to point it out on a map...but that’s probably for the best considering what happened there.
: In this town, no one could speak. Which made passing the time impossible. Which made everything there come to a halt.
: The schools were quiet. The streets were quiet. And even the seasonal festivals were so quiet that you could walk from one end to the other without hearing a pin drop.
: But one day, when a girl from the city showed up, that all changed.
: This girl wasn’t all that remarkable, but she had something no one else from the village had — a voice.
: It was the first time an outsider had even set foot into the city, so the villagers were very cautious. But it wasn’t as if the girl wound up here on purpose, no...
: She’d simply wandered in on accident and decided to explore.
: But she slowly became very uneasy in this new environment...
: And, incapable of finding her way back to the main road, the girl would move from door to door...hoping someone would be able to guide her home.
: But one by one, the doors would open and close. And she’d be turned away before even getting the chance to speak.
: That is...until she came across a towering apartment complex.
: This complex loomed over the village below, casting a shadow on everything else that she’d somehow managed to overlook thus far.
: “There has to be someone there who can help me,” the girl thought, moving ever so closer to a concrete staircase that appeared to expand for miles.
: On the first floor, there was no one.
: On the second floor, she found a cat. But the cat ran off the moment she kneeled down to pet it.
: One by one, she’d scour the perimeter of each floor of the complex, knocking on every single door to no avail.
: And it wasn’t until the 63rd floor that something changed.
: The girl, who had subconsciously remained silent up until this point, opened her mouth to let out an exasperated sigh.
: But when she tried, nothing came out.
: So she tried again. And again. And again. But still, nothing.
: Lost and scared, and having no idea who to turn to or where to go to find her way home, the girl dropped to her knees in anguish and tried to cry out to the sky. But again...nothing.
: Until the sound of a door opening behind her tears her from her pain and loneliness as she shoots her head back to see who was coming to help her.
: To her dismay...it was no one.
: It was just a door.
: “That’s fine,” the girl thought. “There could be someone inside.”
: Again, she tried to speak these words out loud, but it was all just silent.
: Slowly but surely, she crept over to the door. Her mother and father had always told her to be wary around people she’d never seen before, but she didn’t have much of a choice at this point.
: Then she grips the metal frame with tiny, trembling fingers and peers inside!
: But again...
: There is nothing.
: So she takes a step in.
: Then another.
: And another.
: And she opens her mouth again.
: But when she tries to speak, her voice comes from somewhere else.
: So she follows it...whispering every few seconds to guide her.
: And she comes to a room that looks a lot like hers from back home.
: But when she lifts up a picture frame to make sure she isn’t just dreaming, she spots one major difference that helps her realize this isn’t her room at all.
: There was no one in any of these pictures.
: They were taken in the same place and had the same frames...but there was simply no one there.
: Shocked, the girl lets out a gasp! And when she does, she remembers what led her here in the first place.
: Her own voice leaked out of a small wardrobe in the corner of the room...one that she didn’t own — but her mother did.
: “Hello?” she whispered. But again, the voice came from the wardrobe instead...
: Don’t open it! Don’t do it!
: Shh!
: The girl puts her hand on the handle...
scene uhhhhhhhscenegoeshere17
: But when she opens the door, what she sees sends a jolt through her body.
: She was staring right back at herself...
: Aaaaaahhhhh I knew it!
: Or at least what used to be her...the girl in the wardrobe must have been dead for years at this point.
: In a panic, the girl sprinted out of the apartment! She needed to get out of there as soon as possible!
: However...when she made it to the stairs...just as she was about to climb down them...
: She felt a pair of hands on her shoulders.
: They pushed her.
: But as she was falling, she was able to spin her body around and see who it was that pushed her.
: But what she saw, in her final moments before her neck broke and the life drained from her body, shocked her.
: It was no one at all...
: It was the cat.
scene uhhhhhhhscenegoeshere18
: Oh, what an interesting ending! Congratulations, Futaba! You have received a passing grade. That was an excellent first attempt.
: Wait, so...who was the girl in the wardrobe thingy? Was the main character dead the whole time?
: Heheh...that’s the mystery. You’re supposed to think about it.
: She never got to pet the cat...
: What a sad ending...
scene uhhhhhhhscenegoeshere19
: Stories like these rarely have happy endings, Yasu. They’re typically just depressing allegories or parables or things of that nature.
: And you like things like that? But you’re so nice.
: They’re all just stories, Yasu. None of that ever actually happened.
: But what if it did?
scene uhhhhhhhscenegoeshere20
: What if...a girl managed to get lost in a small village where no one could speak and then climbed up 63 flights of stairs to find her body in a wardrobe and be murdered by a cat?
: Yeah...
: What if that happened?
: I...I don’t know, Yasu. I suppose that would be very sad.
scene uhhhhhhhscenegoeshere21
: Well, Nodoka...the floor is all yours. Don’t be too hard on-
: I don’t want to tell a horror story anymore.
: Huh? But that’s the whole-
scene uhhhhhhhscenegoeshere22
: Wha- Nodoka?!
scene uhhhhhhhscenegoeshere23
: It’s just paper. There will always be more.
: But...those were your-
: Futaba, I doubt she even wrote anything in there. She probably just wanted to make a dramatic entrance or something because she thinks it’ll help her win the horror story contest.
: I have no interest in horror. Nor this competition.
: What I want is to tell a love story. So I am going to tell a love story.
: But that’s not what the competition-
scene uhhhhhhhscenegoeshere24
: It all begins inside a block of ice. Or a box of dirt. Or a closet of your grandmother’s clothes. Or anywhere you can exist in a way that is only slightly suspicious and not outright burdensome.
: The protagonist is you. And beside you is a flower. Frozen in time. Finally sprouting. Long deceased and pressed within the arms of a book to prevent rotting.
scene uhhhhhhhscenegoeshere25
: It looked something like this.
: Like what? You’re just standing there.
: Your imagination. Use it.

: Picture yourself in a place you are not meant to be during a time in which you are not meant to exist, full of pretty things that were plucked from out of the ground and put somewhere else for safekeeping.

: You were once beautiful — just like your grandmother’s flowers. But now, you’re incapable of staring down at your hands without paying too much attention to the new lines that are forming. Cracking.
: You’re breaking apart and no one can stop it. Not a block of ice. Not a box of dirt. And wearing your grandmother’s clothes could never make you feel young again.
: But that is fine.
scene uhhhhhhhscenegoeshere26
: And it’s fine because the you who’s someone else and somewhere else has someone else who will see something else. Else the someone you’ve become won’t be someone at all.
: The ice, the dirt, the closet — they all vanish once the sun rises. But in their absence, you find a special place.
: You make the mistake of believing you are human and trick yourself into a dangerous state of mind by reverting to where it is you would have come from should you have actually been born.

: In between the legs of a woman you’d learn to call “mother,” as that is the word that best describes the relationship you have...you’d find a meaning in existing that is greater than simply surviving.
: You would find penitence. Cowardice. And experience the warmth of detached arms, stretching out their skin and covering you like a blanket as you proceed to grow as the rest of the world shrinks.
scene uhhhhhhhscenegoeshere27
: But your dependence on this brand new entity becomes more than a simple longing to be enveloped by Mother’s infinitely expanding arms or the scent between her legs.
: What she is and what she stands for eats away at your preexisting view of the world — reshapes the ideas you formed when you were hardly more than a cautious springtail.
: But where does love come into play? At what point does this become more than the maniacal rambling of a girl you all simply fail to understand because her mind doesn’t work the same way yours does?
: It comes into play in the very beginning. Before all of this. And a child raised by wolves would act more like a dog than a human, don’t you think?
scene uhhhhhhhscenegoeshere28
: The glow of all three moons reforms into one infinite stream of light! Covering the land and helping plants grow while killing off those who learned to walk without its assistance!
: The ice melts! The dirt dries up! And a leak through the bottom of your grandmother’s closet allows in a virus that makes its way up the walls to nest in her blouses unworn!
: But no! This is love! You think that from the bottom of a heart that you are just finding out is real. And you recall your mother’s scent one more time as your body starts to burn up!
: You recall why you think the things you do and how all of the thoughts you had without her were nothing more than misguided delusions or the nightmares you’d eat to fill your belly!
scene uhhhhhhhscenegoeshere29
: But what is a thought if it’s not a thought you think to yourself? And what good is guidance if you’ll be forced to fend for yourself in the years the grass stops growing?!
: These questions eat away at you! So you seek comfort in the arms that open up, but not too much as larger wingspans scare you! You’ve been preyed upon by them before!
: Like a vulture in reverse, you place decaying meat back onto the bones of what has already been killed by the infinite light, and hope that time will reverse its course and bring them back to life!
: But what has already been cut down is not the same as you! You can be picked clean as many times as it takes and still persist as you are the main character! You’ve known that from the start.
scene uhhhhhhhscenegoeshere30
: And what you love is how, at often times, it may feel as if everyone else is simply acting out a play.
: What you love is the person who taught you that life is more than just a block of ice or a box of dirt or the clothes in your grandmother’s closet.
: What you love is the one who thawed you out. Who propagated you. Who dressed you in clothes you could wear with pride.
: And while your feelings are true and your feelings are real, the script says that you are meant to stay frozen...That you’re an ever-blooming tree...And that the bedroom is for other boys.
scene black
: But wait...
: There was something else beside you, wasn’t there?
: A flower...Frozen in time. Finally sprouting- yet long deceased and pressed within the arms of a book to prevent rotting.
: What became of that? Or it? Or her?
: Now, back in the place you once were, where your story both begins and ends...you remember that you were only alone because you forgot to glance over.
: And that the stasis in which you exist, as peculiar and inexplicable as it may be, is your true home.
: It is here where larger wingspans do not terrify you, for you are the apex predator. And you can pick the meat off of any carcass you like.
: The three moons smile down at you. They pat you on the head and call you a good boy. And it is those divine hands that remind you of her one last time.
: But did she ever exist in the first place?
: Or do you just think she did?
scene uhhhhhhhscenegoeshere31
: If that is not love, I don’t know what love is. But I’d ask that you do not hold it against me if my definition of the word differs from yours for I have yet to fully thaw.
: And I still long for someone to steal me away from my own block or box or closet and provide me a purpose as I can not figure one out on my own.
I don’t know how I got here.
: There is nothing more dangerous than being trapped in an empty space with little more than the voices in your head, as they’re the ones pulling the levers and gears inside of you.
I don’t know what I’m listening to.
: But a question no one ever asks is if it's possible to fall in love with them.
: Is it possible to come to enjoy the company you create rather than the company you find?
But I feel compelled to grab her.
: If you can believe it, I think so.
: If you can feel them, I think so.
To cut her into pieces.
: Sometimes, I can’t help but wonder if I’m a voice in someone’s head.
: If there’s someone who takes shelter not in my body, but in the idea of my existence.
And replant them somewhere else.
: And as lonely as that may sound...I like it.
: For it makes my being far more free.
: And it gives me more time to think.
: Nodoka. Can you come with me for a minute?
: This concludes my love story.
: Daddy calls.
